analyst_view.overall: Early view: Augsburg's league games have produced 40 goals in nine, joint-most in the division, and they have scored in every match despite going seven without a win under Manuel Baum. Hoffenheim under Christian Ilzer should be favourites at home but are likely coming off a European midweek, with several defenders out until December or January.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.5 goals. I lean higher: Augsburg score in every game but concede plenty (five at Leipzig), and Hoffenheim's defence is missing Albian Hajdari, Valentin Gendrey and Robin Hranac. Hoffenheim's own league games average close to 3.7 goals.

corners.text: The site expects 10.1 corners. Hoffenheim play with two strikers and Augsburg with wing-backs, which keeps corners around average, and I find nothing that moves the number.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. I lean lower: Hoffenheim took one booking at Bremen and none against Schalke, and Augsburg had no bookings against Freiburg and two at Leipzig. Neither side has been card-prone lately.

shots.text: The site has 33.2 shots, which is high. Hoffenheim's volume and accuracy dipped at Bremen, and European fatigue could slow them, so I lean slightly lower on volume while still expecting goals.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.7 on target. Augsburg's defensive record means opponents usually hit the target, and Hoffenheim have two finishers in Fisnik Asllani and Tim Lemperle, so I stay level.
